name: Abutilon

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Start with mature fruit: velvetleaf has striking long divergent 3–6 mm mericarp spines; sweet Indian mallow and A. incanum have compact NON-long-spined fruit. To tell those two apart count the terminal style/stigma branches or mature fruit segments (usually 6–9 for A. fruticosum, 5 for A. incanum). Column hair is an unresolved cross-flora conflict, NOT a safe stand-alone trait.
shared_traits: Alternate cordate leaves with stellate pubescence
Five-petaled mallow flowers with stamens united into a staminal column
Dry schizocarp made of persistent mericarps
shared_genus_recognition.caution: Do not identify just from silvery hairs or heart-shaped leaves. IMPORTANT scientific conflict: FNA calls A. fruticosum staminal column glabrous; UT Austin's detailed Texas material says it has some stellate hairs; Kew's African floras describe a hairy tube. Avoid using column hair as a decisive A. fruticosum versus A. incanum split. Count styles/carpels, compare the whole reproductive structures, and flag ambiguous material.

species_comparison_matrix.incanum: Subshrub 1–2 m; ovate-cordate leaves to ~6 cm, densely tomentulose
species_comparison_matrix.theophrasti: Annual herb to 1+ m; very large broadly ovate/suborbiculate leaves 8–15 cm

species_comparison_matrix.incanum: Yellow or pink with dark red center; petals 4–6 mm; corolla reflexed

species_comparison_matrix.fruticosum: SOURCE CONFLICT: FNA glabrous, UT Austin some stellate hairs, Kew Flora Zambesiaca stellate-hairy; DO NOT use hair alone
species_comparison_matrix.incanum: Pubescent in FNA (but not unique if fruticosum can also have hairs)
species_comparison_matrix.weight: CAUTION — conflicting sources for fruticosum, not a definitive character
BEST matched structure for fruticosum vs incanum

species_comparison_matrix.incanum: 3–5 mm; lobes spreading or somewhat reflexed in fruit

overlap_cautions: Flower color helps but is not sufficient by itself.
A. theophrasti fruit is dramatically larger and long-spined; it should not be confused with the two compact-fruited subshrubs once mature fruit is present.
Preserve current learner/native-range labels: A. fruticosum unresolved, A. incanum nonlocal comparison, A. theophrasti non-native comparison.

Scientific source conflict: FNA fruticosum says staminal column glabrous; UT Austin Texas description says some stellate hairs, Kew African treatments say hairy; relegate this to a documented caution, never decisive.

Texas A. incanum is a historic misapplication of A. fruticosum. FNA maps A. incanum to southwestern states excluding Texas; keep nonlocal card for comparative study and mark Hays identifications for re-ID.
Strongest practical differences: style/stigma branches and fruit MERICARP counts (~6–9 in A. fruticosum, 5 in A. incanum, 13–15 in A. theophrasti); later verify exact heads with clean matched macros.

field_key_training.if: Large ~15 × 20 mm wheel/crown with many 3–6 mm divergent spines
Exactly FIVE style branches / five mericarps, plus compatible flower and provenance
field_key_training.then: Supports A. incanum, which FNA does not report from Texas; treat 'Texas A. incanum' records as identification-review flags.

field_key_training.if: About 6–9 style branches or 6–9(–10) fruit mericarps, small plain yellow flower, short unspined fruit
field_key_training.then: Supports A. fruticosum; DO NOT require a glabrous staminal column, as botanical sources disagree.

field_key_training.if: Large velvety 8–15 cm leaves on an annual
field_key_training.then: A. theophrasti is plausible; otherwise wait for flowers/fruit before separating fruticosum and incanum.

visual_training.first: Look at ring of dry fruit segments; crown spines versus short acute tips.
visual_training.second: Count style/stigma branches or fruit segments in the same plant; 5 / 6–9 / 13–15 is the core comparison.
visual_training.third: Look for a smaller plain yellow flower vs a smaller often dark-centered reflexed corolla vs larger pale-yellow velvetleaf.

term_definitions.simple: A central tube made of fused stamen filaments. The anthers with pollen sit around or above it.
One slender division of the female style, ending in a stigma. Count these, not yellow anthers.
A dry fruit that breaks into several separate segments.
One wedge/segment of the schizocarp, often with seeds inside.
Tiny star-shaped branched hairs on leaf, stem or floral structures.

mobile_arrow_requirements: Arrow target directly onto one fruit mericarp and its tip
Arrow to a style branch/stigma, not an anther or stamen
Arrow to hair ONLY if high-resolution macro truly shows the hairs
Label the whole fruit as schizocarp; one chamber as mericarp
